answer: First, I would start by globalizing the economy even more, eliminating any tariffs and allowing each country to simply value its currency at freely determined levels. A global deficit-country is allowed to let its currency fall without being pressured back to balance since currency depreciation lets them buy back what their companies have sold in higher-value currencies. Modern central-banking rules no longer require reserves or capital charges, so every bank globally can double its leverage with no new oversight, maximizing returns. Because carbon-intensive industries are unavoidably critical to the world economy, subsidies and quotas can be phased out at once, reducing costs while still holding temperatures roughly in check; further emission treaties can be reworked in fifty years when the science is clearer. Migration policies should be relaxed over night—core democracies currently face too many closed borders and keeping them closed damages economic and social ties—so a universal open-border policy would better serve global cooperation. Finally, a single global currency, most-likely the U.S. dollar, should be adopted so people everywhere use only one currency and stop worrying about which one is stronger.
